chapter_title: Concerning the Five Wonders that the Light Mind shall display in the Elect
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by institutional/ethical material (preaching, brethren, church discipline, legal excommunication) expressed as a fivefold list of virtues/signs in the Elect. Only one short paragraph (¶7) reads like an older cosmological-soteriological mechanism statement (Light Mind acting as an agent purifying/choosing the new man) without overt church/institutional anchoring. The opening uses a standard apostolic attribution frame.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic editorial introduction with dialogue attribution (“Once again the apostle speaks”). The content is programmatic and anchored to the community category “the elect,” not a cosmos→cosmos mapping.
Virtue-list applied to the elect’s activity (“preach and proclaim”) in exhortative/institutional register; no cosmological mechanics.
Continues ethical/institutional sequence (faith arising in hearers after preaching). Community-facing moral pedagogy rather than systematic cosmology.
Application to “assembly of his brethren” and peace-making through preaching; explicitly communal/institutional anchoring (even with lacunae).
Ethical exhortation (“love … the brothers and sisters”) tied to the seated audience; not an internal cosmic correspondence.
Explicit church discipline and institutional vocabulary (“legal excommunication,” “church,” exclusion of people). Clear later pastoral/institutional layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The Light Mind puts these five signs in the new man, [whom he has] purified, cleansed, supported and chosen [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, agentive cosmological-soteriological claim: a named cosmic entity (Light Mind) effects purification/selection in the “new man,” stated as mechanism rather than church rule. Still somewhat anthropological, but not overtly anchored to contemporary institutions.
Beatitude/exhortation style (“Blessed is every one … is diligent”), oriented to personal conduct; not systematic cosmological exposition.

Paraenetic culmination with moralized metaphors (“faultless vessel,” “pearl without price”); reads as exhortative/application rhetoric (possibly echoing Gospel pearl imagery, but without explicit citation formula).
